name: Automation Cache Snapshot Performance Hotfix
changes: Fixes the v3.6.85 Automation load regression caused by rereading and reparsing media-quality-cache.json once per existing episode/movie while recomputing live cutoff state.
Shares one read-only media quality cache snapshot across the complete Automation summary response, including Library cutoff decoration, Wanted, and Calendar.
Fixes Interactive Search stalls by resolving the current file traits once per Search Releases request and reusing that result for every candidate evaluation and automatic-eligibility check.
Reuses one current-file trait snapshot for automatic feed candidate evaluation and the scheduler's post-search safety pass, eliminating candidate-count-dependent cache I/O in unattended upgrades.
Preserves v3.6.85 canonical current-file trait precedence and DV-only to DV+HDR fallback upgrade correctness without reverting the trait-coherency fix.
Preserves v3.6.84 Allow-versus-Prefer cutoff semantics, accurate Wanted reason labels, 1080p Balanced behavior, and 4K preferred dynamic-range progression.
Preserves v3.6.83 installed/runtime/UI update-version coherency and the guarded source commit -> annotated tag -> separate trigger commit release topology.
Preserves frozen Newsgroup Browser tuning, SABnzbd 5.1.2, Smart Import/post-processing, Metadata Server v0.3.3, Diagnostic Collector v1.0.31 and the Defender-clean yEnc pipeline.
regression_guards: A full Automation summary with hundreds of file records must load media-quality-cache.json once, not once per Library/Wanted/Calendar record.
Interactive Search with hundreds of candidates must resolve the current-file trait snapshot once and must not reload media-quality-cache.json per candidate.
Automatic feed evaluation and scheduler safety matching reuse one current-file trait view per target rather than per candidate.
v3.6.85 DV/DV+HDR canonical trait precedence and same-tier dynamic-range upgrade acceptance remain guarded.
v3.6.84 Allow-only dynamic-range policies remain acceptable rather than mandatory upgrade targets, while Prefer/Require continues to drive intended 4K progression.
Generic WEB to explicit WEB-DL source upgrades and base-quality cutoff behavior remain unchanged.
v3.6.83 same-version update protection and installed/runtime/UI version coherency remain guarded.
The canonical Source commit parser, immutable tag topology, frozen browser values, SABnzbd 5.1.2 and Defender-clean yEnc source/build identity remain unchanged.
